title: honua-devops provision approval receipt v1
description: The durable approval that authorizes exactly one Terraform mutation. honua-devops refuses to start an apply or destroy without a valid, unexpired, single-use receipt of this shape from a configured trusted issuer. A caller boolean, an echoed challenge token, or a self-issued receipt is not authorization. This schema describes the document an issuer produces; it is an INPUT contract, and satisfying it is necessary but not sufficient - the signature must also verify under the configured issuer key.

issuer.description: Issuer identity. Must be present in the operator-configured trusted-issuer allowlist; an unknown issuer is refused.

keyId.description: Names which key must verify the receipt, without disclosing it. Derivation depends on signingMode, because a KMS HMAC key has no exportable material to hash: under `local-hmac-dev` it is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the raw symmetric key; under `kms-mac` it is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the UTF-8 KMS key ARN, which both the GenerateMac and the VerifyMac principal can compute from the ARN alone.

planSha256.description: SHA-256 of the saved binary plan this approval authorizes.

planMetadataDigest.description: The honua-iac exact-plan metadata digest. This is the value terraform-exact-apply.sh checks against --approved-digest, and it transitively binds the backend, target account and role, inputs, source revision and prior state - not just the plan bytes.

recoveryContextSha256.description: Optional only for a retained destroy recovery. The normal issuer reads it from the protected plan response and appends newline plus recovery-context-sha256:<lowercase digest> to the ordinary canonical payload. It binds the immutable original-root/parent/next-plan relationship; no old approval is reused.

signingMode.description: How the signature was produced, and therefore whether the receipt is evidence. `kms-mac` computes the MAC in AWS KMS with the capability split across principals: the issuer holds kms:GenerateMac only, the verifier kms:VerifyMac only, and no principal can export the key. `local-hmac-dev` keeps a symmetric key in the verifier's own process, so the verifier can forge anything it accepts - it is a development mode, honua-devops marks its receipts NON-EVIDENTIARY wherever they are reported, and certification (honua-release#129) requires `kms-mac`. This field is covered by the signature, so it cannot be downgraded without invalidating the receipt. A receipt that omits it is refused; the verifier will not guess how a signature was made.

expiresAtUtc.description: Validity ceiling. honua-devops additionally refuses a receipt whose lifetime exceeds one hour.

signature.description: Base64 HMAC-SHA-256 over the canonical payload: the fields schemaVersion, approvalReceiptId, issuer, keyId, provisioningOperationId, planSha256 (lowercased), planMetadataDigest (lowercased), action, stack, environment, decision, issuedAtUtc (round-trip "O" format, UTC), expiresAtUtc (same), signingMode - joined in exactly that order with a single \n between them and encoded UTF-8. Where the key lives, and therefore who can compute this value, is set by signingMode. Native asymmetric issuance (KMS Sign/Verify or Ed25519) remains a post-2026.1 follow-up; see honua-devops#175.
